posts.cooked:
I've been trying to play some games in the Temple of Zhu Long, and I'm curious as to how Rites of Renewal works.  Is it:

(a)  If the heroes discard X cards in a *single* round, they can resurrect a fallen hero at the end of the environment turn; OR

(b) The heroes discard any number of cards they want every turn; once the total number of cards discarded over the course of the game reaches X, they can resurrect a fallen comrade at the end of the next environment turn.

I didn't want to go about discarding cards until I was sure how it worked.

posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
I'm going to confidently say the answer is A. The card reads "At the end of the environment turn," which states the time in which the condition must be met.

At the end of the Environment turn, each player may discard any number of cards. If (H) plus 2 cards are discarded this way, flip an incapacitated Hero character card, restore it to 8 HP, and that Hero's player shuffles their cards into their deck and draws 2 cards.

The "discarded this way" phrase also leads me to believe that the revival happens when that condition is met during the end of the environment turn. This can be easily tested in the video game.

From the last sentence of the very last paragraph of the latest fireside chats:

"Suppose Sky-Scraper is incapacitated and has used the “become a target” incapacitated ability. If she is revived using Rites of Revival, the 1 HP indestructible target status is wiped, and she is her regular self at 8 HP with a 33 HP max and is fully destructible. Rites of Revival essentially resets the character, starting anew."

To me that means everything that the entire deck is restored as if the character was starting over. Full 40 cards regardless of where they may have been right before Revival activated.
